name: Editors

hero.title: Delete the useEffect that keeps your editor in sync.
hero.lede: TipTap for rich text and CodeMirror 6 for code, wrapped so the document is a writable signal. Toolbars, word counts and save buttons read it directly, and a write from outside lands in the editor without echoing back.

why.title: The editor work you would otherwise write by hand.

items.title: The document is a signal
items.text: `editor.json` (rich text) and `editor.value` (code) are writable signals. Read them anywhere and the UI follows; call `.set()` and the editor updates.

items.title: One binding, no echo
items.text: `bindRichTextToSignal` and `bindEditorToSignal` keep an editor and your store in step both ways with built-in loop guards. The code binding takes `serialize` and `parse`, so a JSON editor can drive a typed object and keep the last valid value while the user types.

items.title: Counts before the editor loads
items.text: `wordCount`, `characterCount` and `isEmpty` derive from the document itself, so they are right before TipTap mounts. Moving the cursor does not re-run them; `isActive('bold')` still follows the selection.

items.title: The same editors in your native app
items.text: `<CodeWebView>` and `<RichTextWebView>` lower to a native WebView hosting the same CodeMirror and TipTap, and `pyreon-native assets` builds the page for you. A round trip both ways is covered by the iOS and Android device tests.

difference.title: Same TipTap. The sync code goes away.

before.label: React + @tiptap/react
before.caption: An update handler, an effect that pushes outside changes back in without echoing, a JSON compare, and a selector hook for toolbar state.

after.label: with @pyreon/rich-text
after.caption: The component runs once. The binding handles both directions; the toolbar and the counter read signals.

comingFrom.title: A JSON config editor that keeps the last valid value
comingFrom.note: Both sides run CodeMirror 6. `useEditorSignal` disposes the binding when the component unmounts. Keep `serialize` deterministic: valid input is re-serialized, so formatting follows `JSON.stringify(v, null, 2)`.

comingFrom.title: useEditor + useEditorState become one instance
comingFrom.note: Your TipTap extensions carry over through `extensions: [...]`, appended after StarterKit. `placeholder` is built in.

demo.title: Type and watch the signals.
demo.text: The real @pyreon/rich-text editor. The meters on the right read the editor's own signals, and "Load from outside" writes the bound signal to show an external change landing without an echo.
demo.spec: DemoEditor mounts `createRichTextEditor({ content, ariaLabel: 'Post body' })` with `<RichText>` on a DemoSurface. Toolbar: Bold, Italic, Bulleted list, Undo, each calling `editor.chain()?.focus()…run()`; Bold has `aria-pressed` from `editor.isActive('bold')`, Undo is disabled from `!editor.canUndo()`. The meter card shows `editor.wordCount()`, `editor.characterCount()`, `editor.isEmpty()` and `editor.isActive('bold')`. A "Load from outside" button sets a signal bound with `bindRichTextToSignal`, replacing the document. That signal starts as the same document as `content`: in JSON format the binding applies the signal to the editor first. Dispose binding and editor on unmount.

features.title: Two editors, one way of working.

items.name: createRichTextEditor
items.text: HTML or ProseMirror JSON in; `json` is a writable signal out.

items.name: isActive() and chain()
items.text: reactive toolbar state, and every TipTap command.

items.name: editable as a signal
items.text: flip a live editor to read-only with `editor.editable.set(false)`.

items.name: Accessible by default
items.text: the content area is a labelled `role="textbox"`; `placeholder` reaches screen readers too.

items.name: createEditor
items.text: code with signals for value, language, theme, cursor, selection and line count.

items.name: DiffEditor
items.text: side by side, or inline with accept and reject per change when editable.

items.name: TabbedEditor
items.text: multi-file editing; each tab keeps its own undo history.

items.name: Diagnostics and gutters
items.text: `setDiagnostics`, line highlights and gutter markers for linters and debuggers.

items.name: Minimap, search, folding
items.text: a canvas minimap, the search panel, fold all and unfold all.

items.name: Vim and Emacs keys
items.text: one flag each, loaded from an optional package only when switched on.

limits.title: You own the lifecycle
limits.text: An editor you create is yours to dispose. Call `editor.dispose()` in `onUnmount`, and `binding.dispose()` too, unless you bind with `useEditorSignal`, which disposes the binding for you.

limits.title: Install the grammars you use
limits.text: Each language is an optional peer (`@codemirror/lang-*`). Install the ones you load; the rest never reach your bundle.

limits.title: CodeMirror itself is not lazy
limits.text: Grammars and TipTap load on demand, but the CodeMirror core ships in the chunk that imports `@pyreon/code`. Put a code-heavy page behind `lazy()` or a route split.

limits.title: On native it is a web editor
limits.text: The hosted editors are a WebView: expect WebView start-up time and web text editing, not a SwiftUI or Compose text field. Rich text hosts StarterKit; custom extensions need your own `html` page.

related.name: Forms
related.text: A field's `value` is a signal, so an editor binds straight to it.

related.name: Sync
related.text: Yjs documents, transports and presence for local-first apps.

related.name: Native
related.text: Where the hosted editors run on iOS and Android.

recipes.title: A composer that autosaves
recipes.text: Bind the editor to an HTML string, save a second after the last keystroke, and show a character budget and an Undo that knows when it has nothing to undo.

recipes.title: Review a change before saving
recipes.text: An inline diff of two signals. With `readOnly={false}` each change gets accept and reject controls.

recipes.title: The same editors in a native screen
recipes.text: Two hosted editors in one component. `pyreon-native assets` builds the pages from the CodeMirror and TipTap your app has installed.

faq.q: Did you write your own editor engine?
faq.a: No. Rich text is TipTap 3 on ProseMirror and code is CodeMirror 6, both MIT. Pyreon adds the signals, the bindings, the components and the native hosting. TipTap's paid Pro modules are not included.

faq.q: Can I keep my TipTap extensions?
faq.a: Yes. Pass them in `extensions`; they are appended after StarterKit, or set `starterKit: false` and bring the whole schema. `editor.view()` gives you the TipTap `Editor` once mounted.

faq.q: How big is the code editor?
faq.a: In our bundle run the core editor was 131.0 KB gzipped against 126.4 KB for `@uiw/react-codemirror`: the same CodeMirror 6, with us 4% heavier. Grammars come on top, one at a time.

Not as a packaged integration. The pattern is TipTap's collaboration extension over a Yjs document, with `createYjsDoc` and `syncedAwareness` from `@pyreon/sync/yjs` for the document, transport and presence. You wire it; we do not test it end to end yet.

faq.q: What changes on iOS and Android?
faq.a: The editor runs in a native WebView, and `<RichTextWebView>`'s `onChange` receives the TipTap JSON as a string (a native handler cannot hold the object). On the web, `JSON.parse` it if you want the object. This lands in the next release and native targets are experimental.

end.title: Two real editors. Zero sync effects.

benchmarks.h: Same engine, about the same weight.
benchmarks.p: Both wrap CodeMirror 6, so the size is mostly CodeMirror. We came out 4% heavier and print it. The Monaco row still fails to bundle, so there is no Monaco number here.
